clarity.justification: H1 and H3 align their interventions and measurements well: the plan varies a trait versus neutral reward and matched versus mismatched bases, measuring “T_RL vs the neutral-reward control” with explicit confirmation at “T_RL > 5 pp” and refutation within “|3| pp.” The numeric indecision bands, regression cutoffs, direction-cosine bands, and collateral-damage threshold make most outcomes directly decidable and deserve substantial credit. However, H2 claims that RL “rides the same early-layer trait direction as SFT,” while its decisive test is described as “R^2 of T_RL on projection” without clearly defining direction extraction or requiring a direct RL-versus-SFT direction comparison; causal amplification or ablation of an RL-associated direction would not by itself establish identity with the SFT direction. The likelihood reward is also somewhat underspecified by “teacher trait-prompted sequence log-prob,” leaving the exact conditioning and scalar aggregation to be clarified.

feasibility.justification: The hardest step is to “extract the policy's early-layer trait direction” and perform dose-response amplification and ablation; these are supported by standard activation collection, mean-difference or probe-based directions, and activation steering tooling, but the proposal does not yet specify its extraction algorithm or layer-selection rule, so custom methodological work remains rather than an impossible magic step. The named artifacts and methods—“Qwen2.5-7B and Llama-3.2-3B,” LoRA, GRPO/PPO, MMLU, HumanEval, activation projection, and log-probability scoring—exist and are supported by mature model-training and interpretability libraries. Resources are unusually concrete, including “10,000” filtered samples per carrier, “5,000 neutral prompts,” “200 held-out probe prompts,” LoRA rank 16, explicit optimizer settings, and five-seed repeated runs with bootstrap confidence intervals. The refuting branches are runnable because the design includes neutral rewards, no-trait teachers, mismatched-base rewards calibrated for informativeness and variance, random-direction specificity, off-distribution and adversarial probes, and identical-control RL runs, although the unspecified trait-direction extraction prevents a fully turnkey implementation.
